summary_paragraph: An elderly male with a history of chronic alcohol use, COPD, atrial fibrillation, and prior strokes was admitted for weakness and hypotension. He was found to have recurrent aspiration pneumonia, confirmed by chest imaging, and was treated with IV antibiotics, initially cefepime and vancomycin, then switched to meropenem due to worsening infiltrates. He experienced episodes of atrial fibrillation with rapid ventricular response, managed with IV and then oral metoprolol. A PICC line was placed for antibiotic administration after repositioning due to malplacement. He had transient encephalopathy with slurred speech and facial droop, but neuroimaging showed no acute stroke. Hyponatremia improved with IV fluids and salt tablets. He remained hemodynamically stable, was transitioned to thickened liquids, and discharged to extended care rehab with plans for outpatient follow-up for swallowing evaluation, thyroid function, and electrolyte monitoring.
